newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares weaker in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares weaker in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Singapore shares drifted lower on Monday morning, pressured by institutional selling of blue chip stocks and a lack of retail interest, dealers said.
New listings like Australand garnered more activity in the absence of incentives for larger capitalisation stocks.
"Australand and the newer issues are the only game in town," a local brokerage dealer said, noting that funds were continuing to shift out of Singapore due to lacklustre forecasts.
The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) fell 6.35 points to 1,983.77 at the lunchtime break, while the UOB OTC index was also weaker, down 6.41 at 1,138.99.
Morgan Stanley upgraded Singapore to a "neutral" from "underweight" in a recent strategy report, but dealers said funds were not bullish about Singapore, considering it mainly a hedge.
Australand, a DBS Land unit, debuted on Monday and hit a high of A$1.47 in Singapore, compared with its issue price of A$1.20. The stock fell back at lunch to A$1.42.
Fraser & Neave, a key STII component, was down Singapore 20 cents to S$10.30. Other losers included City Development, down S$0.30 to $13.50 and UOB foreign, off S$0.20 to S$15.10.
